taxonomy.name: Veterinary Clinical Knowledge Graph
taxonomy.description: Production-grade veterinary knowledge graph for GraphRAG/Neo4j. P0-P3 corrections applied: collision-free IDs, full relationship section, foreign-key references, pathogen hierarchy, SNOMED-CT Vet + ICD-10 dual coding, 14 formerly empty node types populated, Breed→Species linkage, Symptom merged into ClinicalSign, DifferentialDiagnosis converted to typed relationships, provenance fields on all clinical nodes.

Epidemiology.name: Incidence
Epidemiology.definition: Number of new cases per population per time unit

Epidemiology.name: Prevalence
Epidemiology.definition: Proportion of cases in population at given time

Epidemiology.name: Case Fatality Rate
Epidemiology.definition: Proportion of infected animals that die

Epidemiology.name: Basic Reproduction Number (R0)
Epidemiology.definition: Mean secondary infections from one case in naive population

Epidemiology.name: Effective Reproduction Number (Rt)
Epidemiology.definition: R0 adjusted for population immunity

Epidemiology.name: Herd Immunity Threshold
Epidemiology.definition: Minimum immune proportion to halt transmission

Epidemiology.name: Attack Rate
Epidemiology.definition: Proportion of exposed animals that develop disease

Epidemiology.name: Sensitivity
Epidemiology.definition: True positive rate of a diagnostic test

Epidemiology.name: Specificity
Epidemiology.definition: True negative rate of a diagnostic test

Epidemiology.name: Positive Predictive Value
Epidemiology.definition: Probability disease present given positive test

Epidemiology.name: Negative Predictive Value
Epidemiology.definition: Probability disease absent given negative test

Epidemiology.name: Odds Ratio
Epidemiology.definition: Ratio of odds of exposure among cases vs controls

Epidemiology.name: Relative Risk
Epidemiology.definition: Risk ratio between exposed and unexposed groups

Epidemiology.name: Outbreak
Epidemiology.definition: Number of cases greater than expected in defined area and period

Epidemiology.name: Endemic
Epidemiology.definition: Constant presence of disease in geographic area

Epidemiology.name: Epidemic
Epidemiology.definition: Disease occurrence clearly above normal expectancy

Epidemiology.name: Pandemic
Epidemiology.definition: Epidemic worldwide or across multiple continents

Epidemiology.name: Zoonotic Spillover
Epidemiology.definition: Transmission of pathogen from animal to human host

Epidemiology.name: Force of Infection
Epidemiology.definition: Rate at which susceptibles acquire infection

Epidemiology.name: Serial Interval
Epidemiology.definition: Time between successive cases in chain of transmission
Epidemiology.formula: mean time symptom onset primary to secondary

PathologicalProcess.name: Acute Inflammation
PathologicalProcess.description: Immediate vascular response to injury with neutrophil infiltration

PathologicalProcess.name: Chronic Inflammation
PathologicalProcess.description: Prolonged inflammation with macrophage and lymphocyte predominance

PathologicalProcess.name: Granulomatous Inflammation
PathologicalProcess.description: Macrophage aggregation into granulomas around resistant agents

PathologicalProcess.name: Coagulative Necrosis
PathologicalProcess.description: Cell death maintaining tissue architecture, protein denaturation

PathologicalProcess.name: Liquefactive Necrosis
PathologicalProcess.description: Dissolution of dead tissue by enzymes or bacteria

PathologicalProcess.name: Caseous Necrosis
PathologicalProcess.description: Cheese-like necrosis characteristic of granulomatous infections

PathologicalProcess.name: Fibrinous Exudate
PathologicalProcess.description: Fibrin-rich exudate in serous cavities or mucosal surfaces

PathologicalProcess.name: Purulent Exudate
PathologicalProcess.description: Neutrophil-rich exudate (pus) in response to bacterial infection

PathologicalProcess.name: Fibrosis
PathologicalProcess.description: Excessive deposition of collagen replacing parenchyma
PathologicalProcess.morphology: Dense collagen, loss of normal architecture

PathologicalProcess.name: Atrophy
PathologicalProcess.description: Decrease in cell or organ size due to disuse, denervation, or malnutrition

PathologicalProcess.name: Hypertrophy
PathologicalProcess.description: Increase in cell size without cell division

PathologicalProcess.name: Hyperplasia
PathologicalProcess.description: Increase in cell number in response to stimulus

PathologicalProcess.name: Neoplasia
PathologicalProcess.description: Autonomous proliferation of cells unresponsive to normal growth controls

PathologicalProcess.name: Metaplasia
PathologicalProcess.description: Reversible replacement of one differentiated cell type by another

PathologicalProcess.name: Dysplasia
PathologicalProcess.description: Disordered cellular differentiation, often precancerous

PathologicalProcess.name: Apoptosis
PathologicalProcess.description: Programmed cell death, non-inflammatory

PathologicalProcess.name: Edema
PathologicalProcess.description: Accumulation of fluid in interstitial spaces or body cavities
PathologicalProcess.cause: Increased hydrostatic pressure, decreased oncotic pressure

PathologicalProcess.name: Hemorrhage
PathologicalProcess.description: Escape of blood from vascular system

PathologicalProcess.name: Thrombosis
PathologicalProcess.description: Formation of intravascular blood clot

PathologicalProcess.name: Infarction
PathologicalProcess.description: Ischemic necrosis from vascular obstruction

PathologicalProcess.name: Shock
PathologicalProcess.description: Systemic failure to maintain adequate tissue perfusion

PathologicalProcess.name: DIC (Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation)
PathologicalProcess.description: Systemic activation of coagulation consuming clotting factors

PathologicalProcess.name: Immunodeficiency
PathologicalProcess.description: Reduced immune system function predisposing to infection

PathologicalProcess.name: Autoimmunity
PathologicalProcess.description: Immune response against self-antigens

PathologicalProcess.name: Hypersensitivity
PathologicalProcess.description: Exaggerated immune response causing tissue damage
